t: Madurai was the capital of the Pandyan dynasty from the 7th century CE, and it passed in turn to the Cholas, the Delhi Sultanate, the Madurai Sultanate, the Vijayanagara Empire, the Madurai Nayaks and the British East India Company in 1801.

The city was built around its temples, and the Nayaks redesigned it as concentric quadrangular streets according to the Shilpa Shastras, a plan that the British kept when they demolished the fortifications in 1837.

Madurai was plundered by Malik Kafur in 1311, fought over in the Carnatic wars and besieged by the English in 1763 and 1764, and in the 20th century it became a centre of the independence and temple entry movements.
dyk: According to the Tamil tradition of the third Sangam, the merit of a poet's work was tested by setting it afloat in the lotus tank of the temple: it was believed that a divine force would make the work of superior merit float and the inferior ones sink.
ev: Megasthenes may have visited the city, which he may have called Methora, and Kautilya mentions it
The Pandyas under Kadunkon oust the Kalabhras
Malik Kafur raids Madurai and plunders the Meenakshi Temple
Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan breaks from the Delhi Sultanate and founds the Madurai Sultanate
The English capture Madurai after a second siege
The Nawab of Arcot cedes Madurai to the East India Company
The British demolish the fortifications around the temple
The temple entry movement is first led at the Meenakshi Temple

f.founded: The city's recorded history is dated to the 3rd century BCE, and the Sangam period settlement site of Keeladi nearby dates to the 6th century BCE.
f.where: On the banks of the Vaigai River, on a flat and fertile plain south-east of the Western Ghats, in Tamil Nadu, India.
f.known: The capital of the Pandyas; the Tamil Sangam, said to have been held there; the Meenakshi and Koodal Azhagar temples; the concentric streets laid out under the Nayaks; the sieges of 1763 and 1764; Gandhi's adoption of the loin cloth in 1921; the temple entry movement of 1939
f.today: Madurai is a major city of Tamil Nadu and the administrative headquarters of Madurai district.
